To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the majority of IBCs express GPR30 and that GPR30 expression correlates with estrogen receptor (ER)-positive status; (2) GPR30 is not an independent prognosticator for overall survival (OS) or disease-free survival (DSF); (3) ER expression is an independent predictor of OS and DFS; (4) co-expression of ER/GPR30 is associated with improved OS and marginally improved DFS.

the role of the estrogen receptor (ER), a nuclear receptor, and GPR30 (a G protein-couled receptor for estrogen) in the development of inflammatory breast cancer (BC).
the study of estrogen receptor expression and its correlation with the prognosis of inflammatory breast cancer.

GPR30 is an important estrogen receptor in IBC and that its expression is an independent predictor of OS.
GPR30 expression in IBC is not associated with poor prognosis.
GPR30 is expressed in a majority of primary IBC tumors and is associated with ER expression, suggesting the possibility that ER and GPR signaling may be active even in ER-negative IHC cases.
